title: Dawn sampler lucidity — weekly serving runtime update
summary: Notes and next actions from this week focused on sampler improvements that reduce KV cache fragmentation and stabilize micro-batching fairness during bursty traffic. Contains quick metrics snapshot, experiment results, open risks, and an action list.
body:
Context:
This week we ran two parallel experiments to address jitter and uneven KV cache utilization observed during morning traffic spikes. The goal: reduce tail latency regressions without losing throughput gains from aggressive coalescing. The work touches kernel scheduling (small change to wake-up granularity), sampler routing (reduce cohort churn), and a KV compaction heuristic prototype.

Highlights:
- Small-kernel wake tweak (+10ms minimum wake window) reduced 99th pct latency from 210ms -> 160ms on the morning spike synthetic test (90th and median unchanged).
- Sampler change (stabilize cohort assignment for 30s) lowered observed KV cache fragmentation score from 0.42 -> 0.27 in shadow runs. Fragmentation metric = fraction of distinct cache segments touched / ideal compactness.
- Micro-batch fairness test: introducing a soft cap per origin lowered queue-jitter incidents by 35% but increased mean batch size by ~4%, net token cost impact negligible in our simulation.

Experiment details and observations:
- Kernel wake tweak (PR #4567): implemented a minimum wake-time of 10ms to avoid excessive context switches for very short windows. Positive in simulated burst but caused slightly higher GPU utilization (2–3%). We think the utilization delta is acceptable for high-priority SLAs.
- Cohort-stability sampler: previously sampler rebalanced cohorts on each prefilling pass which caused a lot of tiny migrations under burst. We now pin assignments for a short TTL (30s) and use a decay to move long-lived cold keys. Shadow runs for 48h showed improved warm-hit persistence.
- KV compaction prototype: background compaction job that consolidates underutilized cache segments every 5 minutes. Useful when fragmentation > 0.4; trade-offs when compaction collides with a traffic surge (spike-window interference). Needs better backoff logic.

Metrics snapshot (test harness, morning spike profile):
- Baseline 99pct latency: 210ms -> with changes 160ms
- Median latency: 38ms -> 40ms (no significant change)
- Throughput: steady at ~5.4k tokens/s across runs
- Cache hit rate: 78% -> 82% after cohort-stability
- Fragmentation score: 0.42 -> 0.27
- GPU utilization: 61% -> 64% after wake tweak

Open issues / risks:
1) Compaction race: compaction job can collide with peak prefill, causing transient increased evictions. Need to add spike-aware suspension.
2) SLO decision: wake-time tweak is beneficial for p99 but increases GPU utilization; product needs short guidance on whether p99 improvement justifies cost.
3) Canary coverage: shadow runs have been promising but we need a narrow canary on dedicated clusters (region-eu-west) to validate under real traffic shape.

Decisions made this week:
- Proceed with wake-time tweak in canary with a per-cluster toggle. If canary passes p99 and cost delta <7%, roll to other clusters. (Owner: Luis Ortega)
- Enable cohort TTL = 30s in all shadow deployments; observe for 7 days.
- Keep compaction prototype behind a feature flag and add spike-sensing backoff before enabling it in canary. (Owner: Maya Patel)

Action items and owners (short list):
- Luis: deploy wake-time toggle to eu-west canary by 2029-04-10; monitor p99, GPU util, throttles. (Jira: RWI-7890)
- Maya: implement compaction backoff (pause if incoming request rate > 2x baseline for 30s), unit tests and run in shadow by 2029-04-12. (Jira: RWI-7921)
- Connor: extend sampler telemetry to include "cohort-churn" metric and surface in console dashboard by 2029-04-15. (dashboard ticket linked in sheet)
- Zoe: cost analysis to product recommending thresholds for wake-time rollouts; deliver a short memo on expected monthly cost delta for Dedicated customers by 2029-04-13.

Meeting notes (standup cadence, 2029-04-05):
- Quick sync with SRE and product about the visibility needed for cost-vs-latency tradeoffs. Product asked for a simple toggle that surfaces expected p99 delta before enabling.
- Operations asked for runbook additions to explain how to revert wake-time quickly if we see GPU thermal alarms.
- Research suggested a follow-up experiment: adaptive wake-time tied to queue depth instead of a fixed TTL. We'll queue that for exploratory spike lab.

Loose brainstorm snippets (informal):
- Could we leverage per-model affinity to keep hot prefixes on a smaller set of shards to improve cache compaction probability?
- Try a hybrid cohort TTL where small-key cohorts get longer pins, large-key cohorts shorter pins.
- Explore hardware counters for more deterministic prefill window sensing.

Attachments / small notes:
- Synthetic harness config used for these runs is in the linked GH PR.
- Short clip of profiler traces available in the slack thread RWI-ops (linked).

Closing thoughts:
The combination of a small kernel wake-time floor + cohort stabilization appears promising: meaningful p99 reduction and better cache warm persistence without material throughput loss. The primary remaining engineering work is hardening compaction backoff and getting product buy-in on the cost/latency toggle. Next week the focus is canary rollout for wake-time and getting cohort churn metrics visible in the console.

Record of edits:
- 2029-04-04: initial draft of experiment results (Asha)
- 2029-04-06: added compaction risk notes and updated metrics (Maya)
- 2029-04-08: action owners and dates added after standup (Luis)
